claim: The guard repairs supplied-value failures on fresh items
estimand: difference in joint-pass rate, guard minus first pass (machine labels)
population: 1,872 supplied-cue targets, 4 models, fresh confirmation items

claim: A supplied cue restores the dropped commitment
estimand: share of outputs honouring the dropped cue, chip minus bare (speech act)

claim: People supply the cue when it matters (cue supply q)
estimand: share of judgments choosing the cue-restored draft when keywords lost the speech-act cue
population: 36 items x 2 judgments, 9 adult annotators (not AAC users), speech act only
design: blind choice between draft pair, item-cluster bootstrap

claim: Listeners pick the intended reading more often with a cue chip
estimand: difference in P(intended reading chosen), chip minus bare
population: 120 messages, 20 adult non-AAC listeners judging stored text
design: paired by item, crossed listeners, two-way cluster bootstrap (frozen)

claim: The cue lowers the consequential error of a listener
estimand: difference in P(response implied by the opposite reading), chip minus bare
difference in P(opposite reading chosen), chip minus bare
design: as row 4; frozen primary, not confirmed

claim: Guard repairs are about as usable as untouched outputs
estimand: difference in usable share, repaired minus control (item consensus)
design: frozen hash-ordered list, Newcombe CI, margin -10 pts

claim: Cue outputs carry what the writer meant
estimand: difference in writer-named intended version, chip minus bare
population: 200 outputs of the writers' own pairs, 20 writers

claim: A cue tap is the cheapest route to stored-text coverage
estimand: difference in H-cov, chip G1 minus bare G1
population: 100 items, 20 writers judging their own pairs

claim: A cue helps a person who uses AAC and a listener (chain L1-L4)
estimand: s x q x G: gain in listener success per message if the cue is supplied
population: people who use AAC and their partners (no data)
design: projection from rows 3-4; AAC link unmeasured
estimate: worst 0 (s = 0); central 14.7 pts (s = 1); best 31 pts (s = 1, q = 1, upper end of row 4)
